newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia diesel fuel rebate cap not needed - govt.
newsitem.headline: Australia diesel fuel rebate cap not needed - govt.

text.p: The Australian government said on Friday it had reached an agreement with the mining industry which meant plans to cap the diesel fuel rebate scheme were no longer necessary.
Finance Minister John Fahey and Resources Minister Warwick Parer said estimates from the industry indicated the 1997/98 budget rebate estimate of A$812.9 million would not be exceeded.

"Thus no action such as a capping mechanism will be necessary to contain diesel fuel rebate scheme expenditure beyond the measures already agreed with industry and now legislated," the ministers said in a joint statement.
They said industry representatives had agreed at meetings in June to provide accurate budget statements for the government.
The scheme provides a rebate to farmers and miners for diesel fuel used for off-road use. The long-standing diesel tax was orginally intended for use on road building and maintenance.
Payouts to miners blew out to an estimated A$823.4 million in 1996/97 from an original budget projection of A$749.8 million.
